# Appendix A2: Using VS Code {#sec-appendix-a2 .unnumbered}

This appendix assumes you've completed [Part 0](../chapters/chapter_00.qmd) —
Python installed, `.venv` created and active, packages installed via
`pip install -r requirements.txt`. Everything below is specific to
working with this book's code in Visual Studio Code.

## Install VS Code and the Python extension

Download VS Code from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com),
then open the Extensions panel (`Ctrl+Shift+X` / `Cmd+Shift+X`) and
install **Python** (by Microsoft).

## Open the project folder

`File > Open Folder...` and select the
`llm-ft-drilling-completions-book` folder you cloned in Part 0.

## Select the virtual environment as your interpreter

Press `Ctrl+Shift+P` / `Cmd+Shift+P`, type **Python: Select
Interpreter**, and choose the `.venv` you created in Part 0 (it will be
listed as a recommended interpreter for this folder).

**Expected result:** the bottom status bar shows `.venv` (or
`Python 3.11.x ('.venv')`) instead of a system Python.

## Run a chapter script

Open `book/code/chapter_01/load_local_model.py` and press the ▶ **Run**
button in the top-right corner, or right-click inside the editor and
choose **Run Python File in Terminal**. Output appears in VS Code's
integrated terminal.

## Run the tests

Open the Testing panel (flask icon in the sidebar) and click **Configure
Python Tests**, choosing `pytest` and the `book` folder. Tests then
appear as a tree you can run individually or all at once.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause |
|---|---|
| VS Code doesn't offer `.venv` as an interpreter | Make sure you opened the repository root (or `book/`) as the workspace folder, not a parent folder. |
| `ModuleNotFoundError` when running a script | Confirm the selected interpreter (bottom status bar) is `.venv`, not a system Python. |
